newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon credit ratings "very close" - source.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon credit ratings "very close" - source.

text.p: Credit rating agencies from the United States, Europe and Japan are in the final stages of preparations for granting Lebanon a credit worthiness rating, a government source said on Thursday.
The four agencies are Moody's Investor Services and Standard and Poor's Corporation of the United States, Nippon Investor Services of Japan and the European company IBCA, the source told Reuters.
"Lebanon is expecting ratings...it's very close. The four companies came here in November and December and we are in the final stages of the process," he said.
However, the source was unable to confirm a report from a Beirut market source that the ratings would be announced between February 15 and 20.
"We don't know the date yet. They have promised it will be done but they are still requesting information....They have set a target date but we have not decided when an announcement will be made.
"This depends on a government decision whether to put them all together or issue them separately," the source said.

Ratings granted by the agencies determine the overall credit worthiness of a borrower. A top rating means there is thought to be almost no risk of the borrower failing to pay interest and principal and allows it to obtain the best loan terms on the international market.
